spec: Which systems cannot run without firmware — the half a libretro .info cannot state. A core declares firmware one file at a time with firmwareN_opt, a format with no way to say 'one of these three' and no way to say 'this system does not start without one of them'. An author who knows a PlayStation needs one regional BIOS therefore has two lossy moves, and the deployed catalogue takes both: Beetle PSX marks scph5500/5501/5502 required and RetroArch then LABELS all three 'Missing, Required', SwanStation marks all five of its images optional and RetroArch labels none of them required. RetroArch labels rather than refuses — at the pinned revision a79435a core_info_list_update_missing_firmware has TWO callers, menu/menu_displaylist.c:880 and ui/drivers/ui_qt.cpp:1238, and both build display rows rather than loading anything. Separately, and NOT as a pinned-source fact: the setting that would block a load, check_firmware_before_loading, reads 'false' in both configurations RetroDECK ships. That name appears nowhere in the source at a79435a; it is read from the deployed 1.22.2 build's binary and its two config files. The dates run the opposite way to the obvious guess: the pin was committed 2026-07-23 and the deployed build was built Nov 20 2025, so the setting is absent from the NEWER source and present in the OLDER build, which reads as [D] upstream having removed it. Separately, and pre-existing: this repo's RetroArch pin is newer than the RetroArch this machine runs. That is what makes the observed refusal the CORE's rather than the frontend's, and it is the contradiction this table records. atlas reports 'need' straight from firmwareN_opt and so reproduces the declaration faithfully, which over an all-optional PlayStation reads as 'nothing required' about a system that will not boot. This table records the missing half as world knowledge, and it records it about the SYSTEM rather than about the core, because that is where the fact lives: mGBA, snes9x and gambatte declare everything optional and so does swanstation, but swanstation says it about a machine observed refusing to start — and whether those three are right is not stated here: of them only gambatte's systemname ('Game Boy/Game Boy Color') is recorded at all, as open, while mGBA's is a third distinct string ('Game Boy/Game Boy Color/Game Boy Advance') with no entry and snes9x's has none either. Entries are keyed by the libretro 'systemname' string VERBATIM, not by an ES-DE system id, because systemname is the unit the .info catalogue groups firmware by and therefore the unit the tripwire's derivation produces; translating into atlas's own vocabulary is not free ('Game Boy/Game Boy Color' is one systemname over two catalogue systems), so the answer that reads this table makes the translation at its own edge (atlas.firmware.system_firmware_system), through the same systemname map an answer's requirements already came through — which means a key naming several machines reaches the one id that map rules for it and not its siblings, narrower than the entry rather than wider. 'verdict' is one of three: 'cannot-run-without-firmware' (no firmware, no boot), 'runs-without-firmware' (the system starts with none present), and 'open' (nobody has established which). 'open' is a real value and not an absence — it is how a system whose cores disagree leaves the tripwire without anyone pretending to know, and it is why six of the seven entries here exist at all. 'evidence' is the repo's own level for the verdict ([V] verified, [D] derived, [O] open) and is tied to it: an 'open' verdict carries [O] and nothing else carries [O], because a verdict that states something cannot rest on an open question and an open question cannot claim a verified reading. 'source' says what the level rests on, in the marker vocabulary the other tables use ([V-live] an observation on a real machine, [V-binary] a read of the shipped core, [V-script] the arrangement's own scripts). 'cores_supplying_an_alternative' names the cores whose all-optional declaration is CORRECT for a system that needs firmware, because the core itself supplies a way to run without a file — PCSX ReARMed's HLE BIOS is the case this table was written around. It is what keeps a system's requirement off a core carrying its own substitute: the answer reads it, and a core named here is reported 'core-supplies-an-alternative' where its unexcused siblings are reported 'cannot-run-without-firmware'. It is not what makes the tripwire's derivation pass: that derivation compares whole systems and never consults this field, so removing it changes no verdict there and only leaves the staleness check with nothing to compare. Cores are named the way the catalogue names them — the .info stem without _libretro — which is what the answer joins on, so a standalone emulator has no spelling here and can never be excused. It appears only on a 'cannot-run-without-firmware' entry, where the question 'is this core understating?' can arise at all, and each core names its own reason rather than being a bare exemption. The list is NOT a completeness claim: it exempts the cores whose alternative has been established, and a core absent from it is a core nobody has looked at, never a core judged to be understating. Today one system carries a verdict. The other six are the disagreements the tripwire in tests/test_system_firmware_tripwire.py derives from the deployed catalogue, recorded as open so that they are visible rather than merely unrecorded, and that tripwire is what keeps this file honest: it recomputes the disagreements at run time and fails when it finds one this file does not carry.

PlayStation.source: [V-live] Observed on a RetroDECK installation with no PlayStation BIOS present: SwanStation never starts, and Beetle PSX refuses at load and names scph5501.bin on screen. [V-binary] Read off the shipped swanstation binary: it registers three region BIOS PATH slots (swanstation_BIOS_PathNTSCJ, _PathNTSCU, _PathPAL), and every value each of those three offers is a BIOS image file name (scph5500.bin / scph5501.bin / scph5502.bin, psxonpsp660.bin, ps1_rom.bin) — none of them stands for running without an image. [D] The catalogue states the same requirement lossily in both directions: of the eight entries declaring firmware under systemname 'PlayStation', duckstation, mednafen_psx and mednafen_psx_hw declare the three region images required, while pcsx1, pcsx_rearmed, pcsx_rearmed_interpreter, pcsx_rearmed_neon and swanstation declare every image optional — one machine, one requirement, and a per-file flag that can express neither 'one of these' nor 'none of these will do'. [O] What is deliberately NOT claimed: both Beetle cores also register a skip_bios switch ('disabled'/'enabled') and an override_bios whose values are 'disabled', 'psxonpsp' and 'ps1_rom' rather than file names, and what either does with no image present has not been observed. Four of the eight declaring entries (duckstation, pcsx1, pcsx_rearmed_interpreter, pcsx_rearmed_neon) have no binary deployed here, so their options have never been read at all. The verdict rests on the [V-live] observations together with the [V-binary] swanstation reading above, and on no reading of any switch.

cores_supplying_an_alternative.pcsx_rearmed: [V-binary] The core registers pcsx_rearmed_bios with the two values 'auto' and 'HLE'. [V-live] It was observed starting and playing a game through on a machine with no PlayStation BIOS present, which is the whole of the evidence for this exemption. Three limits ride with it. Which of the two values was in force during that run is not recorded, and nothing here establishes what 'auto' does when no image is present. The core is not claimed to be the ONLY PlayStation core that can run without one: the Beetle cores register a skip_bios switch nobody has observed, and four of the eight declaring entries have no binary deployed here, so their options have never been read. And what the exemption now does: an answer reads it, so PCSX ReARMed is reported 'core-supplies-an-alternative' and keeps requirements_met true over a machine with no PlayStation BIOS, where its unexcused siblings are reported 'cannot-run-without-firmware' and report false. Remove the exemption and that core goes red with them.

Saturn.source: [D] The deployed catalogue disagrees with itself: kronos, mednafen_saturn and yabasanshiro each declare a required file, and yabause declares everything optional. [O] Nothing has been observed on a machine and no core option has been read, so whether a Saturn starts with no firmware present is unestablished.

This key is one systemname over two catalogue systems, which is the spec's own reason for keying by systemname rather than by an ES-DE id.
